fixes.before: Anyone who enjoys being outdoors and is curious about practicing meditation in nature. Register once for the listed season. Weather cancellations are communicated to registered participants by email; check your email before setting out and pass updates to any guests you have invited.

fixes.before: Jesse Foy facilitates this group with an emphasis on peer discussion and shared practice. A topic chosen by the group or guiding teacher gives us a focus for the hour. When Jesse is away, members support the discussion together. The session closes with a short lovingkindness practice. Register once to participate in this ongoing group.
fixes.after: Each Thursday, we gather around a specific dharma topic and spend an hour in peer-to-peer dialogue, shared practice, and honest reflection. The emphasis is on understanding the teachings through your own experience, not just learning about them.

fixes.before: Join us for meditation, followed by a community gathering with refreshments and conversation. The registration form collects attendance plans; contact RIM if you need to clarify how to take part.
fixes.after: Join us for a special drop-in practice, followed by a warm and welcoming gathering with refreshments, conversation, and good company.

fixes.before: Through guided meditation, time in nature, reflection, and conversation, we will explore CARE in the midst of change. There is time to know our experience, meet it with curiosity, and practice responding with care.
fixes.after: Through guided meditation, time in nature, quiet reflection, and conversation, we will practice cultivating awareness, appreciation, releasing, and beginning again.

fixes.before: Qigong (chee-gong) is a traditional Chinese practice combining slow movement, meditation, and breathing. Within RIM’s community, this movement tradition supports attention to the body and the practice of caring for ourselves. It offers another setting for the awareness and care we explore through CARE.
fixes.after: Qigong (chee-gong) is a traditional Chinese health practice that combines slow, gentle movements with meditation and breathing. It’s a way of listening to your body and giving it friendly, supportive care — with no previous qigong experience needed.

fixes.before: This group meets monthly from May through October at Menomonee Park. Each gathering lasts about 75 minutes and includes a slow walk, guided meditation, and time to share reflections. The walk includes uneven terrain; the preparation notes below can help you decide whether it fits your needs.
fixes.after: This group meets monthly from late spring through fall for walks at Menomonee Park. Each gathering lasts about 75 minutes and includes a slow, mindful walk on easy trails, guided meditation, and time to share reflections. The pace is gentle, the trails are manageable, and the company is good.

fixes.before: Practice outdoors with the ground underfoot and the sounds of wind and water. Walking and meditating together lets us explore CARE through contact with the body, the natural world, and one another.
fixes.after: Practice outdoors with the ground underfoot and the sounds of wind and water. Walking and meditating together gives us time to notice our surroundings and how we meet them.

fixes.before: Build supportive friendships with fellow practitioners
fixes.after: Build genuine friendships with fellow practitioners (kalyana mitta — spiritual friendship)

fixes.before: This weekly group studies Buddhist teachings on suffering, change, compassion, and freedom. We explore what they help us see in our own experience and how that understanding informs CARE. Study gives us ways to examine familiar reactions and bring greater care into daily life.
fixes.after: The Buddha’s core teachings — on suffering, impermanence, compassion, and freedom — aren’t abstract philosophy. They’re practical observations about how our minds work and how we can live with more clarity and less unnecessary struggle. This weekly study group is a place to explore those teachings together.

fixes.before: This Sunday gathering gives us time to practice kindness, compassion, joy in others’ happiness, and equanimity, or steadiness through change. These heart practices support CARE in how we meet our own experience and the people around us.
fixes.after: Kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity (steadiness through change) aren’t just nice ideas — they’re capacities we can strengthen through practice, the way we’d strengthen a muscle. This short Sunday session is dedicated to that practice.

fixes.before: Each Monday morning, guided practice and short teachings explore lovingkindness, compassion, joy in others’ happiness, and equanimity, or steadiness through change. Buddhism calls these the four immeasurables. Conversation gives us room to explore how they develop in daily life.
fixes.after: Each Monday morning, we practice meditations rooted in the four immeasurables — lovingkindness, compassion, joy in others’ happiness, and equanimity (meeting change with steadiness and care) — with guided practice, short teachings, and conversation about how to carry this into daily life. The tone is friendly and unhurried.

fixes.before: Lovingkindness is a practice of deliberately offering warmth to ourselves, to people we love, and to people we find difficult. We explore this aspect of CARE through guided meditation and conversation about how we meet ourselves and others.
fixes.after: Lovingkindness is a practice of deliberately offering warmth — to yourself, to people you love, and even to people you struggle with. It’s simpler than it sounds, and the effects are real.

fixes.before: Saturday mornings at RIM bring guided meditation and a dharma talk, a teaching drawn from Buddhist wisdom and applied to everyday life. Together we explore CARE: knowing what is happening in our experience, meeting it with kindness, and carrying that understanding into how we live with others.
fixes.after: Saturday mornings at RIM are a place to slow down, sit together, and listen. Each session pairs guided meditation with a dharma talk — a teaching drawn from Buddhist wisdom and applied to the real questions of how we live, how we relate, and how we meet difficulty with steadiness and care.

fixes.before: Meditation develops through practice, patience, and guidance. This weekly gathering offers instructions as we meditate and time for questions. We explore CARE through settling, awareness, and a kind attitude toward what we find, whether we are beginning or have practiced for years.
fixes.after: Meditation is a skill — one that develops with regular practice, patience, and skilled guidance. This weekly drop-in is a place to learn that skill from the ground up, or to deepen a practice you’ve already begun.
